story: Gilgamesh journeys to meet the flood hero Utnapishtim, who tells him a secret story. In the city of Shuruppak, the great gods Anu, Enlil, Ninurta, Ennugi, and Ea swore to send a flood, but Ea secretly warned Utnapishtim through a reed wall, commanding him to demolish his house and build a boat to preserve living things. Utnapishtim built a large boat with six decks, sealed with bitumen, and loaded it with silver, gold, his relatives, craftsmen, and all the beasts and animals of the field. A storm arose, sent by the gods, with thunder, wind, and flood lasting six days and nights, destroying all humans and covering the land. The gods, frightened by their own act, wept in the heavens. When the storm calmed, Utnapishtim's boat rested on a mountain. He released a dove, a swallow, and finally a raven, which did not return, showing the waters had receded. He then offered a sacrifice, and the gods gathered around it. Enlil was angry that anyone survived, but Ea rebuked him for the disproportionate punishment. Enlil then blessed Utnapishtim and his wife, granting them immortality, and sent them to live far away at the mouth of the rivers. Later, Utnapishtim challenges Gilgamesh to stay awake six days and nights, but Gilgamesh fails, falling asleep immediately. Utnapishtim then tells him of a plant at the bottom of the sea that restores youth. Gilgamesh retrieves it but loses it to a serpent while bathing, which sheds its skin and departs rejuvenated. Gilgamesh returns empty-handed to Uruk, where he admires the city's great walls.
